restoration_note: The teaching describes how the cycle of regeneration (ⲡⲧⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ) passes through the discrete degrees of the rational (ⲛⲁⲓⲍⲙⲉ, firmaments / spiritual heavens) without tearing them and without mingling with what they hold. The wheel's motion is illustrated by a ship parting lions at its prow and a bird ascending without leaving a track in the air. Most gaps are single-letter or short morphological completions where the editor's restoration is constrained by visible traces (gap 4 = ⲙ in ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲩ; gap 5 = ⲓ̈ⲉⲩⲉ completing ⲙⲙⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲉⲩⲉ 'lions'; gap 6 = ⲍ ending ⲕⲟⲟⲍ; gap 7 = ⲱⲧ qualitative; gap 8 = ⲉ; gap 9 = ⲙⲟⲩ in ⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ̄ 'joined'; gap 10 = ⲱⲩ in ⲍⲱⲱⲩ 'themselves'). Gap 0 is the chapter-title noun phrase; gap 1 the closing chapter-number marker. Only gap 2 is substantive: a prepositional phrase before ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ describing where the Wheel courses, restored at moderate confidence based on parallel locative constructions in the same teaching.

coptic_restorations.basis: Editor's restoration with ⲡⲧⲣ visible. The whole teaching turns on the relation between the Wheel (ⲡⲧⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ, the cyclic process of regeneration) and the heavens/firmaments (ⲛⲁⲓⲍⲙⲉ, the discrete degrees), as the body of the teaching makes explicit (lines 4-7, 21-23). The pairing matches the question structure of the chapter.
Standard Kephalaia heading layout: chapter number repeated as closing marker after the title.

Approximately 9 characters; the gap supplies a locative phrase governing ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ ('cosmos'). The same teaching uses ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲙⲏⲧⲉ ⲛ̄- ('in the midst of') in line 16 (ⲍⲛ ⲧⲙⲏⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ⲙ̄ⲙⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲉⲩⲉ) for the ship's motion through the lions, exactly the figure being applied here to the Wheel's motion through the cosmos. The cosmos here = the natural mind taken as a whole through which the cycle of regeneration revolves.
Editor's restoration; only initial ⲕ physically lost, ⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ visible. Lexicon term: the natural mind in formation, the structured field through which the cycle of regeneration moves.
Single missing letter completing ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲩ ('them'), the object of ⲛⲟⲩⲭⲉ ('cast'); editor's restoration confirmed by syntax and surrounding visible letters.
Plural ending of ⲙⲙⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲉⲩⲉ ('lions') from visible ⲙⲙⲟⲩ-, exactly matching the form already attested in line 9 of this teaching.
Single final letter completing ⲡⲉϩⲕⲟⲟⲍ ('his place / stand'); editor's restoration is unproblematic.

Editor's restoration giving the qualitative ⲉⲧⲭⲱⲧ ('which is stretched/extended') from visible ⲉⲧⲭ-. Fits the figure of the prow-piece set fast at the front of the ship, around which the lions are parted; in correspondence, the rational stretched through the natural as the cycle's leading edge.
Single line-initial letter; editor's restoration. Probably the prefix beginning the temporal clause that follows.

Initial syllable completing [ⲙⲟⲩ]ⲭⲧ̄ ('joined / mingled together'), the standard lexicon form for ⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ. Here the lions rejoin behind the ship — the natural's strong loves close again behind the cycle's passage.

Editor's restoration completing ⲍⲱⲱⲩ ('themselves'), the reflexive split across line break (ⲍⲱ- / -ⲱⲩ). Required by the parallel construction with the preceding clause ('the Wheel does not cleave the heavens, nor do the heavens themselves mingle with the Wheel').

english_segments.core_english: as it turns and as it courses {1}.
at the front of the ship, cleaves the lions, casting them
to this side and to that — every hour separating the lions
of that ship, opening (a way) to those (lions) at his place which is {2},
and at that very hour, before any delay comes, the
lions are {3} with one another upon the head of the ship; and the
{4}, the heavens, mingle inward with the Wheel.

english_restorations.basis: Coptic gap 0 = ⲡⲧⲣⲟⲭⲟⲥ ⲙⲛ ⲛⲁⲓⲍⲙⲉ; gap 1 is the closing chapter-number marker (no English correlate). The body of the teaching (lines 4-7, 21-23) explicitly thematizes both terms together. Lexicon: 'Wheel' = the cyclic process of regeneration; 'heavens' here = the firmaments / discrete degrees of the rational.

english_restorations.proposed_english: in the midst of this cosmos
english_restorations.basis: Gap 2 = ⲍⲛ̄ ⲧⲙⲏⲧⲉ ⲙ̄ⲡ ('in the midst of the'), gap 3 = ⲕⲟⲥⲙⲟⲥ. The phrase 'in the midst of' is the same construction used in line 16 of this teaching for the ship moving through the lions, here applied analogically to the Wheel's motion through the cosmos (the natural mind in formation).

Coptic gap 7 = ⲱⲧ giving qualitative ⲉⲧⲭⲱⲧ. Fits the prow-figure: the leading point of the ship is the place 'which is stretched out / extended,' parting the lions. Coptic gap 6 (the final ⲍ of ⲡⲉϩⲕⲟⲟⲍ) is fully covered by 'his place' in the surrounding English and needs no English placeholder of its own.

Coptic gap 9 = ⲙⲟⲩ completing ⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ̄ ('joined / mingled together'). Lexicon: the lions rejoining behind the ship corresponds to the strong loves of the natural closing again after the cycle has passed through, leaving no track.

Coptic gap 10 = ⲱⲩ completing ⲍⲱⲱⲩ ('themselves'), forming the second half of the parallel ⲟⲩⲧⲉ ⲛⲧⲁⲩ ⲍⲱⲱⲩ ('nor do they themselves'). Translates the line-break reflexive together with its grammatical introduction so the English reads as one clause.
